This 2016 BMW X5 Was Over $70,000 New, Just Sold $10,850
17 photos
Photo: Cars&Bids
If you dream about buying a cool third-generation BMW X5 , then this is your sign, because the value of this model has started reaching new lows.
In fact, the pictured example initially retailed for $70,845, and as mentioned in the title, it recently changed hands on the used car market, fetching $10,850. Thus, it has lost almost $60,000 in roughly one decade.
You are looking at an xDrive35d BMW X5 from the 2016 model year, which means that it packs a 3.0-liter inline-six turbodiesel under the hood. The N57 mill was good for 255 hp (258 ps/190 kW) and 413 pound-feet (560 Nm) of torque when the SUV was new, with the peak thrust available between 1,500 and 3,000 rpm, and the maximum output at 4,000 rpm.
Everything is channeled to the rear-biased xDrive all-wheel drive system through a smooth-shifting automatic transmission with eight forward gears. This model is clearly not a sprinter disguised as a premium mid-size SUV, but it took a very respectable 7+ seconds to push from 0-60 mph (0-97 kph), independent tests back in the day revealed, and had a 130 mph (210 kph) electronically limited top speed.
Other diesel versions included the xDrive40d and the M50d, with 309 hp (313 ps/230 kW) and 376 hp (381 ps/280 kW), respectively, as well as the xDrive30d, xDrive25d, and sDrive25d (RWD), which had 255 hp (258 ps/190 kW), 228 hp (231 ps/170 kW), and 215 hp (218 ps/160 kW), respectively. The lineup also included the sDrive and xDrive35i, xDrive40e, and xDrive50i, with 302 hp (306 ps/225 kW) for the former two, and 308 hp (313 ps/230 kW) and 444 hp (450 ps/331 kW) for the latter two, respectively.
Photo: Cars&Bids The X5 M sat at the top of the family, packing a 4.4-liter twin-turbocharged V8 engine with 567 hp (575 ps/423 kW) and 553 lb-ft (750 Nm) of torque, reaching 62 mph (100 kph) in 4.2 seconds. The X5 M Competition had 617 hp (625 ps/460 kW), and dropped the sprint time to 3.9 seconds. With the optional M Driver’s Pack, the X5 M hit 180 mph (290 kph).
This BMW X5 xDrive35d has a Mineral White Metallic paint finish and a Mocha interior. It features the M Sport Package, the Premium Package, Driver Assistance Package, Driver Assistance Plus Package, Cold Weather Package, Dakota leather upholstery, and a panoramic sunroof, the listing shows.
It has never been involved in an accident, but according to the seller, the rear bumper was replaced almost one year ago, after a car backed into its right rear corner. The usual chips and scratches and some dings on the outside, a crack in the left lower front bumper, curb rash on the wheels, weathered finish around the center caps, some corrosion on underbody hardware, wear on the seats and interior surfaces, and leaking front strut are the known flaws.
The BMW X5 in question had 120,900 miles (194,600 km) on the clock at the time of cataloging, so it is not exactly a low-mileage example. It had its four tires replaced in March 2025, and the engine oil and filter were changed in April 2024. Moreover, it also had its brakes serviced, coolant flushed, and intake manifold gasket replaced in October 2026, and the engine oil and filter changed in May 2026.
Photo: Cars&Bids Additional services entries were recorded in October 2025 and January 2025. In the former, the vehicle had its differential fluid, rear differential fluid, and transmission fluid flushed, the water pump and air filter replaced, the brakes serviced, and the engine oil and filter changed. And in the latter, it had its engine oil and filter changed, the brake fluid flushed, and the fuel filter and fuel tank module seal replaced.
Besides the vehicle , the new owner will get the factory all-weather floor and trunk mats, two keys, a front license plate mount, and the owner’s manuals. The seller says to have purchased this ride in February 2020, and they added some 44,200 miles (71,100 km) before parting ways with it for pennies on the dollar compared to the initial selling price.
But how much would an xDrive35d variant of the 2016 BMW X5 cost you in today’s used car market in the States? That would be between $11,500 and $16,500. Dealers could ask more, pushing the price into the $20,000 territory, and the trade-in value of this thing is said to be between $8,500 and $10,500. And for just under $11,000, the pictured machine is definitely a lot of car for the money.
Thus, all we can say is congrats to the buyer for scoring a great family hauler for basically nothing. The X5 in question was advertised on Cars&Bids, where the online auction ended on October 27, 2026. And if you want to see it in more detail, then you can do that here . However, before you head over to the listing, let us know if you would have bought this SUV for $10,850.
